39 A nucleus of magnesium-23 decays to form a nucleus of sodium-23, emitting a + particle and
particle X.
What is particle X?
A
an antineutrino
B
an electron
C
a neutron
D
a neutrino

hints: Notice the wording $\beta^+$ particle - this is a positron with charge $+1$ emitted when magnesium-23 with proton number $12$ becomes sodium-23 with proton number $11$.
Connect this to conservation of lepton number: the positron carries lepton number $-1$, so particle X must carry lepton number $+1$ to keep the total at zero.
Compare the two light particles in the options: $\beta^-$ decay with an electron is paired with an antineutrino, so $\beta^+$ decay with a positron needs the opposite partner.
walkthrough: Write the decay with nucleon numbers and proton numbers: $^{23}_{12}\text{Mg} \rightarrow ^{23}_{11}\text{Na} + ^{0}_{+1}\beta + \text{X}$. Nucleon number $23$ is unchanged and charge $+12 = +11 +1$ is already balanced.
This shows a proton in the nucleus has changed into a neutron: $p \rightarrow n + ^{0}_{+1}\beta + \text{X}$. Particle X must therefore have zero charge and almost zero mass.
Apply lepton number conservation. Before decay the lepton number is $0$. The $\beta^+$ positron has lepton number $-1$.
To return the total to $0$, particle X must have lepton number $+1$ and carry away some of the decay energy.
Recall the pair for $\beta^-$ decay: $n \rightarrow p + e^- + \text{antineutrino}$. The mirror $\beta^+$ process uses the antiparticles: $p \rightarrow n + e^+ + \text{neutrino}$.
Therefore particle X is a neutrino. This is option D.

A.explanation: An antineutrino is emitted with $\beta^-$ decay alongside an electron, not with $\beta^+$ decay alongside a positron.

B.explanation: An electron has charge $-1$ and would not conserve charge with the $\beta^+$ particle already emitted.

C.explanation: A neutron has nucleon number $1$, so emitting it would change the total nucleon number from $23$ to $24$.

D.explanation: A neutrino conserves lepton number and energy in $\beta^+$ decay where a proton changes to a neutron and emits a positron.
